lawyer:
Khan Saifur Rahman, Advocate, instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record-s ----- For the Petitioner.

Not represented ----- Respondent Nos. 2-5.
parties:
Abdul Rashid  ------ Appellants
Vs
Santi Bhusan Deb and others  ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mohammed Fazlul Karim, J: This petition for leave to appeal at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against the impugned judgment and order dated 31- 5-2001 making the Rule absolute, dismissing the suit, setting aside the judgment and decree of the Courts below decreeing the suit for specific performance of contract. 

 4. The suit was decreed and on appeal the same was affirmed. It appears from the impugned judgment that on 3-5-2000 the High Court Division discharged the Rule but the matter was subsequently taken up for further hearing on 27-5-2001 and the impugned judgment was delivered on 31-5-2001 upon hearing the learned Advocates of the parties and made the Rule absolute dismissing the suit directing defendant to deposit Taka 85,000 being Taka 50,000 as earnest money and Taka 35,000 solatium within four months in the trial Court and the plaintiff will be at liberty to withdraw the same and in default the petitioners will get more three months to deposit the said amount with interest as per rate of Sonali Bank at the relevant time and in default the decree passed by the Courts below shall stand. 

 8. The said bargain is uneven and unconscionable and learned trial Court and the Court of Appeal below could not be indifferent about the uneven stipulation entered into between the parties in the matter of ultimate dispose of 1.02 acres of land for only Taka 50,000 in case the executant failed to get the deed executed by the cousins in respect of rest 0.42 acre thereby forfeiting Taka 1, 32,000 which includes certain unapportioned amount from out of their share. The jurisdiction for a decree of the specific performance of contract is discretionary and the Court is not bound to grant such relief merely because the plaintiff has proved the agreement. In view of the forfeiture clause, the unconscionable bargain and uneven stipulation between the parties, the Court of law in exercise of discretion could not decree the suit for specific performance of contract. The High Court Division has, however, allowed Taka 35,000 as solatium while dismissing the suit and the defendant has not moved against the said granting of solatium. 

 16. Thus the judgment that has been delivered, signed and sealed, thereafter the same cannot be changed and the only recourse for any alteration, addition, modification, etc in the judgment/ decree/order is for the Court to hear the matter under section 152 or on review on the ground specific in Order XLVII rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
